holidays.name: National Chocolate Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the silky, spoonable delight of chocolate pudding, whether it comes from a cup, a box mix, or a lovingly stirred saucepan. Skin-on-top lovers and skin-haters may now debate.
holidays.origin: One of many unofficial American food days, popularized by food-celebration calendars and social media rather than any formal proclamation. Pudding itself has roots in medieval English boiled puddings, and the creamy chocolate version took off in the 20th century with boxed mixes.
holidays.funFact: Early 'puddings' were often savory and boiled in animal stomachs or cloth bags. The sweet chocolate cup we love today is a far more pleasant evolution.

holidays.name: National Beautician's Day
holidays.description: An unofficial day to thank hairstylists, makeup artists, and other beauty professionals who keep the world looking sharp and who also double as unlicensed therapists.
holidays.origin: An informal observance in the United States honoring the beauty industry, circulated through trade groups and salon communities. It is not tied to any government declaration.
holidays.funFact: Many hairstylists report that clients often confide more in them than in close friends, which is why the chair has been called the cheapest therapy couch around.

holidays.name: International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking
holidays.description: A serious United Nations observance with a global focus on tackling drug problems, supporting prevention, and promoting treatment and recovery. Events include campaigns, public talks, and community outreach worldwide.
holidays.origin: Established by the UN General Assembly in 1987 and first observed on June 26, 1988. The date was chosen to commemorate Lao Tzu's reputed connection to opposing the opium trade in China, though the historic link is debated.
holidays.funFact: The day is marked every year with a World Drug Report from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime, which is a surprisingly hefty annual data-packed publication.

holidays.name: Beautiful Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to noticing, creating, and appreciating beauty in everyday life, from sunsets and street art to a perfectly brewed cup of coffee.
holidays.origin: An informal, feel-good observance that circulates on holiday calendars and social media, encouraging people to pause and savor small beautiful things, with no single known founder.
holidays.funFact: Studies on 'awe and appreciation' suggest that deliberately noticing beautiful things for even a few minutes a day can measurably lift your mood.

holidays.name: Pink Flamingo Day
holidays.description: A day for flamingo fans to celebrate the iconic bird and its plastic lawn-ornament cousin by adding a splash of tacky tropical pink to yards, parties, and outfits.
holidays.origin: The plastic pink flamingo was designed by Don Featherstone in 1957 for Union Products, and kitschy flamingo celebrations have spread through lawn-decor and retro culture ever since.
holidays.funFact: Real flamingos are born gray and only turn pink because of pigments called carotenoids in the algae and crustaceans they eat.
